featured.title: Mesa de Ayuda — Helpdesk
featured.tagline: A full-stack ticket management system with RBAC, JWT auth and Zod validation. 25 automated tests, green CI and Helmet security headers.
featured.imageAlt: Screenshot of the Mesa de Ayuda dashboard with KPIs and the ticket list
featured.problem: Small support teams (2–10 people) often track requests across email, chat or spreadsheets. Mesa de Ayuda centralizes status, priority, ownership and basic metrics as a lightweight alternative to Zendesk or Freshdesk. It's a portfolio project, not a production service: no SLAs, audit history, SSO or durable multi-instance storage.
featured.decision1Body: Zero infrastructure; atomic writes (temp + rename) reduce the chance of partially written files. Trade-off: no queries, transactions, indexes or multi-instance coordination, and concurrent writes can overwrite each other. For production I'd migrate to SQLite, then PostgreSQL.
featured.decision2Body: Stateless auth with 8-hour tokens and a process-local Set of revoked IDs. Trade-off: the list resets on restart and isn't shared across instances; the client clears its local state but never calls the API logout endpoint. Production would need Redis or server-side sessions.
featured.decision3Body: Simple scope and fast iteration: routes, auth, validation and ticket logic in backend/src/server.js, with JSON I/O isolated in store.js. Trade-off: hard to unit-test in isolation (tests spawn HTTP servers). Post-MVP: split into routes/controllers/services.
